title: Hybrid iterators: cursor expiry, resume semantics, retry/backpressure guidance for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD for Hybrid Iterators: define a consistent, cross-language client contract for paginated fetches and streaming responses that supports resumable iteration, graceful rollback during partial failures, and clear retry/backpressure behavior. The goal is to provide SDK primitives for Python, TypeScript, and Go that enable: (1) efficient cursor-based pagination for large result sets, (2) resumable streaming iterators that can continue after transient disconnects, (3) safe retries with idempotency guidance for non-idempotent endpoints, and (4) a compatibility/migration plan for existing clients. This document clarifies scope, outlines acceptance criteria, and records trade-offs for the engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose a unified iterator primitive that supports .next()/async iteration and returns an object with: data, cursor (opaque token), expiration_ms, and optional resume_token.

Cursor semantics documented: server can return either 'cursor' (opaque opaque-token) or 'offset' fallback; clients prefer cursor when present and fall back to offset semantics only if server advertises 'offset' capability.

Resume behavior: if an in-flight stream disconnects with a transient network error (5xx, connection reset, context deadline), client will attempt up to 3 resumptions using resume_token within expiry window; each resume attempt uses exponential backoff starting at 200ms and capped at 2s.

Backpressure and flow control: streaming iterators support an opt-in max_in_flight_messages parameter; TS/Go use pushback via transport-level windowing (SSE/WebSocket/HTTP2) where available; Python offers a buffering queue with optional blocking on .next() when queue full.

Retry contract: SDKs implement an idempotency-key helper and clearly mark non-idempotent routes; default automatic retries are only enabled for idempotent requests (GET/list/stream-resume). Non-idempotent POSTs must be retried explicitly by user or via a safe wrapper provided by SDK.

Compatibility: introducing the unified iterator primitive must not break existing sync iteration patterns; provide adapter shims (e.g., legacy_list_generator()) in each SDK for 12 months and log warnings when used.

Test coverage: end-to-end tests for resume after transient disconnect, cursor expiry behavior, offset fallback behavior, and client-level backpressure across Python/TS/Go are in CI with simulated server-side failures.

Documentation: migration guide, example snippets for pagination/resume in Python/TS/Go, and a troubleshooting section with common error codes and recommended user actions are published in the SDK docs site.

Telemetry: SDK emits standardized metrics/events for resume_attempts, resume_success, cursor_expired, retries_per_request and backpressure_blocked_count; events are recorded with tenant_id anonymous hashing and sample rate default 1% (configurable).
notes: Scope clarifications: this ticket is limited to SDK surface and client-side helpers. Server API changes (cursor shape, resume_token generation) are handled in ENG-1842 and must be coordinated; not in scope here.
Edge cases: if resume_token is missing but server returns a new cursor, clients must not attempt resume and should restart from the new cursor if semantics allow. Documented as 'no-resume' case.

Cursor expiry trade-off: short expiry reduces server state but increases resume failures; we propose default expiry_ms=300000 (5 minutes) with server-side TTL override. SDK exposes client_max_resume_window to tune behavior.
Idempotency guidance: generate idempotency keys client-side for user-initiated mutations where retry is desired; provide helper middleware for common languages to auto-add idempotency-key when safe.
Streaming protocols: prefer HTTP/2 for long-lived streams where available; fall back to chunked transfer (HTTP/1.1) or SSE. TLS and connection pooling notes in language-specific implementation doc.

Migration path: provide opt-in beta flag in SDK 2026.04 to enable unified iterator; GA in 2026.10 after telemetry review. Deprecation warnings for legacy iterators begin at GA and continue for 12 months.
Accessibility: ensure async iterator ergonomics in TS and Python match idiomatic language patterns (for-await-of in TS, async for in Python, channel-style pattern in Go).
decisions: Use opaque server cursor as primary pagination primitive; offset as documented fallback only.
Support both synchronous and asynchronous iterator APIs in Python and TS; Go will provide channel-based iteration and helper Next() that returns (item, err).
Default client retry policy: allow automatic resume/retry for idempotent fetch/stream-resume operations only; mutation endpoints are opt-in for retries using idempotency-key helpers.
Expose configuration knobs: max_resume_attempts (default 3), initial_resume_backoff_ms (default 200), max_resume_backoff_ms (default 2000), max_in_flight_messages (language default 64).
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize API surface and add design PRs for Python/TS/Go SDKs (interfaces, names, and examples).
Week 2: implement core iterator primitive in TS and Python with adapters for legacy helpers; stub telemetry events.
Week 3: implement Go channel-based iterator and Next() + context-aware cancellation.
Week 4: integration with server-side cursor/resume endpoints (coordination with ENG-1842).
Week 5: e2e tests for resume, expiry, offset fallback in simulated flaky network environment; performance benchmarks for buffer/backpressure settings.
Week 6: docs, migration guides, telemetry dashboards, and OSS release candidates.
Post-GA: deprecation warning roll-out and monitoring of resume_failure_rate; iterate on defaults based on telemetry.
followups: Work with console team to surface resume_failure_rate and cursor_lifetime distribution in runtime dashboards (Console-2321).
Define server-side cursor TTL defaults and admin override API in ENG-1842; add compatibility matrix for older server versions.
Add an advanced section to SDK docs on building robust consumer patterns (prefetching, bulk-resume patterns).
